h2: Radiographic testing in Detroit: NRC licensing in Michigan and what it means for your job
html:
Radiographic testing in Detroit: NRC licensing in Michigan and what it means for your job

Michigan is not an NRC Agreement State, so industrial radiography with gamma sources in Detroit is licensed and inspected by the NRC itself, through its Region III office in Chicago, while the state handles X-ray equipment. That split decides who regulates an RT job in metro Detroit. Before any Detroit RT job, Atlantis confirms which license and reciprocity route applies and how the radiography will be arranged.

Who regulates what in Michigan. Under the NRC's arrangement, Michigan keeps jurisdiction over X-ray equipment, naturally occurring radioactive materials and certain radioactive materials that are not produced in a reactor, with the Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (EGLE) Radiological Protection Section as the state contact. Sealed gamma sources such as iridium-192 and cobalt-60, the workhorses of field radiography, are byproduct material under NRC licensing and the industrial radiography rules in 10 CFR Part 34. In practice:

  • X-ray cabinet and real-time radiography of castings inside a plant falls to the state's X-ray program
  • Field gamma radiography on refinery piping, power plant welds and structural steel falls to the NRC
  • A crew licensed by an Agreement State, such as Ohio, Indiana, Illinois or Wisconsin, that brings a source into Michigan works under the NRC's reciprocity provision in 10 CFR 150.20, filing NRC Form 241 before the work starts
  • At a temporary job site, a certified radiographer must be accompanied by at least one other qualified radiographer or radiographer's assistant

When you compare RT suppliers for a Detroit job, ask for the license that covers the source, the reciprocity filing if the license was issued by another state, the radiographers' certifications, and the employer's SNT-TC-1A certification of the same people for film interpretation. Those are four different documents, and an audit can ask for any of them.

Where radiography fits in the local mix. Metro Detroit's manufacturing base radiographs castings and safety-critical parts in production, often by digital or real-time X-ray, where cycle time and image storage matter more than portability. Plant and utility work, by contrast, uses portable gamma or X-ray sources on piping, vessel and boiler welds during planned outages. An exclusion zone is far easier to hold when a unit is down and the area is clear, so plant radiography is usually booked into the outage schedule or into off-shift hours.

When another method fits better. Digital radiography shortens exposures and removes chemical processing; TOFD and phased array UT remove the radiation boundary altogether where the construction code and the client allow ultrasonic examination in place of RT. The method itself, including what radiography finds and misses, is explained on the radiographic testing page, and mixed-method outage scopes start from NDT inspection services.

Detroit-area technicians learning the method can use the RT training course for SNT-TC-1A theory and the Practical NDT radiography simulator to practice exposure and image interpretation; radiographer certification for radiation safety is a separate step. Local enrollment is on the Detroit NDT training page. For a Detroit quote, list the welds or parts, wall thicknesses, the hours the area can be cleared and the governing code in the Detroit RT request.
